title: A Converging Strategy for the Generation of a Virtually Sequenced cDNA Library from Unreferenced Pacific Oysters
protocol: Obtain oyster specimens.
Keep oysters on ice during postharvest period, transport, and prior to laboratory use.
Process oysters within 4-7 days after purchase.
Cut out approximately 100 mg of homogeneous soft tissue from the approximate geometric center of each specimen with a sterilized scalpel.
Transfer the samples into liquid nitrogen.
Euthanize the remaining part of the oysters by freezing at -80 °C for 1 h and discard as biological waste.
Grind the flash-frozen oyster tissue into a fine powder in a mortar filled with liquid nitrogen.
Weigh out 75 mg of each specimen’s frozen tissue into a sterile 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Mix with 1 mL of guanidinium thiocyanate-phenol extraction reagent.
Centrifuge the sample at 14,000 x g at 4 °C for 15 min.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 200 µL of chloroform and mix thoroughly by using a vortex mixer for 10-15 s until the mixture turns milky-white.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g at 4 °C for 15 min.
Transfer the upper aqueous layer carefully with a 200 µL pipette without disturbing the interphase into a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 500 µL of isopropyl alcohol and mix samples gently by inversion.
Leave the samples for 20 min on ice.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g at 4 °C for 8 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend each pellet in 1 mL of 75% EtOH.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g at 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove all of the supernatant.
Repeat step once.
Dry pellets for 6 min at room temperature.
Dissolve dried RNA pellet in 25 µL of DEPC-treated water and keep tube on ice.
Use RNA samples within 24 h.

Prepare a reaction mixture using a commercial reverse transcription system: Add 4 µL of MgCl2 solution, 2 µL of 10x Reaction Buffer, 2 µL of dNTP solution, 0.5 µL of RNase inhibitor, 0.7 µL of AMV Reverse Transcriptase, 0.5 µL of Oligo(dT) 15 primer, 1 µL of the extracted RNA sample and 9.3 µL of H2O into a 300 µL PCR tube.
Incubate mixture in a PCR Thermocycler for 60 min at 42 °C.
Increase temperature to 95 °C for 5 min.
Store generated cDNA library at -20 °C for up to 12 months.
Prepare PCR mixture using a 10 µL pipette.
Add 0.25 µL of high-fidelity DNA polymerase.
Add 2 µL of dNTP solution (2.5 mM each).
Add 0.5 µL of COX1 or ND forward primer (100 µM).
Add 0.5 µL of corresponding COX1 or ND reverse primer (100 µM).
Add 1 µL of cDNA library.
Add 5 µL of 5x buffer solution.
Add 16 µL of distilled H2O into a PCR tube.
Perform initial denaturation at 95 °C for 5 min.
Cycle through annealing at 55 °C (30 s), elongation at 72 °C (2 min), and denaturation at 95 °C (30 s) for 35 cycles.
Perform final elongation step at 72 °C for 5 min.
Use 5 µL of PCR product to verify by agarose gel electrophoresis.
Observe amplified COX1 or ND gene as a single band at either 759 or 748 base pairs, respectively.
Purify the rest of the PCR product with a PCR clean-up kit.
Add 100 µL of solution 'PCR-A' (DNA binding buffer) to the sample.
Vortex briefly to mix contents.
Place the purification column into a 2 mL centrifuge tube.
Pipette the reaction mixture of 4.4.1. into the column.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 1 min at room temperature.
Discard the filtrate from the centrifuge tube.
Return the column to the 2 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 700 µL of solution 'W2' into the column.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 1 min at room temperature.
Discard the filtrate and return the column to the 2 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 400 µL of solution 'W2' to the column.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 1 min at room temperature.
Pre-heat 1 mL of deionized water to 65 °C in a metal block heater.
Transfer the column into a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Pipette 25 µL of the 65 °C hot pre-heated deionized water to the center of the white column membrane.
Let the membrane soak for 1 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 1 min at room temperature and discard the column.
Store the purified PCR product for up to 12 months at -20 °C.
Send the purified PCR samples from step 4.5 for Sanger sequencing using the relevant COX1 or ND forward primers as sequencing primers.
Optionally, use the COX1 or ND reverse primers for bidirectional sequencing.
Compare the sequences with the genome sequence of the Pacific oyster reference strain using NCBI Nucleotide BLAST online tool.
Amplify and purify the MgUGD gene using PCR with specific primers.
Transfer 2 µL of digestion buffer (10x concentrated) into a centrifuge tube.
Add 6 µL of deionized water to the centrifuge tube containing digestion buffer.
Combine 10 µL of purified MgUGD PCR product, Nde I restriction enzyme (1 µL, 20 U), and Xho I restriction enzyme (1 µL, 20 U) in a new centrifuge tube.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 3 hours.
Prepare predigested pET-30a vector by transferring 500 ng of pET-30a vector into a centrifuge tube.
Top up the volume to 16 µL with deionized water in the tube containing the pET-30a vector.
Add 2 µL of digestion buffer (10x concentrated) to the pET-30a vector mixture.
Combine Nde I restriction enzyme (1 µL, 20 U) and Xho I restriction enzyme (1 µL, 20 U) with the pET-30a vector mixture.
Incubate the pET-30a vector mixture at 37 °C for 3 hours.
Add 1 µL of alkaline phosphatase (1 U) to the predigested pET-30a vector after 3-hour incubation.
Incubate the pET-30a vector with alkaline phosphatase at 37 °C for an additional hour.
Inactivate the alkaline phosphatase by heating the mixture at 75 °C for 10 minutes in a pre-heated metal block heater.
Transfer 4 μL of the digested MgUGD or MgUXS DNA products into fresh 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Add 4 μL of the digested pET-30a vector.
Add 1 µL of Ligation Buffer (10x).
Add 1 µL of T4 ligase (3 U).
Incubate the reaction mixture at 22 °C for 3 h.
Transform electrocompetent E. coli Mach1 Competent Cells by electroporation using the ligation products.
Spread the transformed cells on LB agar plates containing 50 μg/mL kanamycin.
Incubate cells at 37 °C for 16 h.
Verify colonies for the desired insertion by Sanger sequencing using the plasmid-specific T7 promoter and terminator primers.
Prepare plasmids from the validated bacterial clones.
Transform E. coli BL21 (DE3) Competent Cells with plasmids bearing the MgUGD and MgUXS genes.
Spread the transformed cells on LB agar plates containing 50 μg/mL kanamycin.
Incubate cells at 37 °C for 16 h.
Cultivate a single colony in 5 mL LB medium with 50 μg/mL kanamycin overnight.

Transfer the culture into 400 mL LB medium and continuously shake at 200 rpm at a temperature of 37 °C until the optical density at a wavelength of 600 nm (OD600) reaches an absorption of approximately 0.5.
Reduce the incubation temperature to 20 °C.
Add 400 µL of isopropyl β-D-thiogalactopyranoside (concentration 1 M).
Induce the expression of the recombinant proteins for 3 h.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at 4,500 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Suspend pellets in 10 mL of lysis buffer (100 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris/HCl, 1% Triton X-100, 1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF), pH 8.0).
Disrupt cells by sonication for 20 min (40 on/off cycles with 20 μm amplitude for 15 s at 4 °C).
Centrifuge the disrupted cell mixture at 14,000 x g at 4°C for 20 min.
Collect the supernatant from the centrifugation step for the activity test.

Incubate 2 µL of the cell lysate with 2 µL of UDP-glucose (10 mM), 4 µL of NAD+ (10 mM), 4 µL of MgCl2 (10 mM), 2 µL of Tris/HCl buffer (500 mM, pH 7.5), and 6 µL of deionized H2O in a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 30 min to perform the activity assay of MgUGD.
Incubate 2 µL of the cell lysate with 2 µL of UDP-glucuronic acid (10 mM), 2 µL of Tris/HCl buffer (500 mM, pH 7.5), and 14 µL of deionized H2O in a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 30 min to perform the activity assay of MgUXS.
Quench the reactions by adding 20 μL of methanol and 40 μL of chloroform to each mixture.
Vortex the sample mixtures after adding methanol and chloroform.
Centrifuge the quenched samples at 14,000 x g for 6 min at 4 °C.
Collect the upper aqueous layer from each tube after centrifugation.
Analyze the reaction products using MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry in negative ionization mode in the m/z range from 500-700.
Mix 1 μL of sample mixture with 1 μL of 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid sample matrix (1% w/V in 50% aqueous acetonitrile).
Observe the expected m/z values at 579 and 535 for UDP-glucuronic acid and UDP-xylose, respectively.
